_comment: Exactly what this extension needs from Audiobookshelf. If upstream changes any of it, the extension breaks in a way that looks like an empty book list or covers with no strips rather than an error - so it is listed here, the API shapes are asserted against the recorded fixtures beside this file by TestContract in tests/python/test_absh.py, the whole of it is exercised against a real server by tests/real at both ends of the supported range, and tools/check_upstream.py quotes it into the issue it opens.

endpoints.used_for: Settings naming the server's version, and saying when it is older than the oldest supported
checking that the URL and API key work
the folder an upload goes into
fetching a book to copy to the player
fields: accepts the API key as an Authorization: Bearer header
returns a single audio file, or a zip for a multi-file book
Content-Type contains "zip" for the multi-file case
endpoints.note: Audiobookshelf also takes the key as ?token=, but a key in a URL ends up in logs and proxies, so it is never sent that way (store/PRIVACY.md).

endpoints.used_for: uploading a book that is only on the player
fields: multipart: library, folder, title, author, series, file0..n

endpoints.used_for: the tests only, making a key the way a user does; added in v2.26.0, which is why that is the oldest supported

page.relies_on: [id^="book-card-"] or [id^="item-card-"] elements whose Vue component (el.__vue__) has libraryItem.id
page.used_for: which book each cover strip belongs to, telling two versions of one title apart

page.relies_on: [id^="cover-area-"] inside the card, sized in em so the strip can sit clear of its menu
page.used_for: putting the strip on the cover rather than over the title under it

page.relies_on: /item/<id> routes, and its Play button as button.abs-btn.bg-success (a hidden one also sits in the select-many bar)
page.used_for: Copy to / Remove from the player, under Play

page.relies_on: a single-page app on one origin (window.$nuxt.$router), reached from the server's root
page.used_for: why the page script registers for the whole origin

page.relies_on: /api/libraries/{id}/personalized returning a bare array of shelves with entities[]
page.used_for: learning titles and ids from what the page already fetched
